name: QNAP TL-D1600S
source: QNAP TL-D400S/D800S/D1600S user guide (tl-dx00s-ug-04-en.pdf): rear SFF port 1 = HDD1-4, port 2 = HDD5-8, port 3 = HDD9-12, port 4 = SSD1-4; front bottom row HDD1..HDD8 left to right, top row HDD9..HDD12 then SSD1..SSD4; card: QXP-1600eS-A1164 (ASMedia switch with four ASM1164, QNAP subsystem vendor 1baa); the earlier QXP-1600eS with a Marvell 88SE1475 is not matched

calibration.note: Measured 2026-11-08 on one unit with a blink test (each disk read for 20 s, the LEDs read at the front; all 16 bays consistent). port_to_position is a fact of the card: each ASM1164 serves one group of four bays in reverse port order, its port 1 (lowest ata port) = the highest bay of the group. card_port_to_group depends on how the four cables are plugged between card and enclosure: this list is the measured unit's cabling, for the card's controllers in PCI address order (there 03:00.0 = HDD9-12, 04:00.0 = SSD1-4, 05:00.0 = HDD1-4, 06:00.0 = HDD5-8). On another unit it is a default until confirmed with Locate; a plugin passes the confirmed cabling of a unit as the 'cabling' option.

host_view: Fans: run by the enclosure itself, from its fan switch at the back (Auto follows the enclosure's own temperature; High, Medium and Low are fixed). The server sees no fan speed or enclosure temperature.
LEDs: the status and drive lights are driven by the enclosure. Locate makes a drive's activity light flash by reading the drive.
Drive temperatures and SMART: the values Unraid reads from each drive, as for any other drive.
Firmware: the enclosure's LCD shows its name and firmware version (press Enter). Updating it needs QNAP's own JBOD Manager; nothing here writes to the enclosure.
Power: switch the enclosure on before the server, as QNAP's guide describes.
